text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- The Confederation of Danish Industries forecasts marked rises in trade with Denmark's seventh largest trading partner Japan due to its expected renewed economic growth and market restructuring. Denmark sold goods worth 10.4 billion crowns to Japan in 1995, importing for only 6.4 billion crowns and exports to Japan are seen at some 12 billion crowns in 1996.
--- Denmark's windmill industry increased its world market share to 60 percent in 1996 from 45 percent in the previous year.
--- Danish banks' ongoing deposit account interest rate war is escalating with Denmark's largest bank, Den Danske Bank, upping rates on a number of bank accounts.

--- Danes are hesitating in investing in Danish shipyard Danyard, part of shipping group J. Lauritzen, because Malaysian Penang Shipbuilding Construction, which recently bought 48 percent of Danyard, could become the shipyard's largest shareholder.
--- In Denmark, bond loans are now the most common type of house financing, outdoing traditional mortgage credit loans.
